backlog.item: Training with carried state between a user’s windows
backlog.why: Moved up 10-18 (user): full-history context at short-window speed (2,048 windows ~5x faster than 32k). Designed, CPU prototype exact; code started 10-18

backlog.item: Teacher targets from the fork’s full-history replay
backlog.why: Needed with carried state; 5.2 h GPU, 3.7 GB

backlog.item: State compression trained in (QAT) at ~400/400 bits per card/note, during the final decay only
backlog.why: Post-training test: 60× smaller state than int8 for +0.0012 / +0.0023 nats. Redo only the final decay from epoch 10 with the compression in the loop. Sped up: fused GPU kernel, no eigensolver (same codec, bitwise on real states); CPU projection 75–80 min. A 10-min GPU benchmark decides the launch

backlog.item: Muon optimizer for the student
backlog.why: Outside pointer: largest instant gains (−0.0005 instant at d=32); our student is AdamW only

backlog.item: Label-free reference: the fork fine-tuned with review type switched off
backlog.why: Honest best a big model can do without review type. Fine-tune first: a cheap from-scratch fork-size retrain lost +0.0037 / +0.0043 in outside runs

backlog.item: Deployment-realistic scoring without the duration leak
backlog.why: Intervals as Anki knows them when it shows the card; both models, cheap. Outside runs: +0.0002 / +0.0004 cost

backlog.item: Exact kernel work for the w64 width
backlog.why: w64 still ~21% slower than the w32 fast kernels at short windows; bit-for-bit identical

backlog.item: More parallel windows at long lengths (8,192 × 8)
backlog.why: Timing test first, then a learning-rate check

backlog.item: Real-timestamp inputs (card age, time since any review, creation batch)
backlog.why: Outside pointer: about −0.0005 / −0.0008 net of the clock leak; needs the dataset build with timestamps

backlog.item: Long-history summary inputs for short windows
backlog.why: Card prior reviews, FSRS state, user pass rate; modest prior

backlog.item: Robustness to other apps: pass/fail-only ratings, no durations
backlog.why: Same test as the review-type one, CPU

backlog.item: Grade-order sanity: interval(Again) ≤ Hard ≤ Good ≤ Easy
backlog.why: Measure how often the student breaks it; enforcing it cost +0.002 on curve in outside runs

backlog.item: Open tuning queue from outside research (Muon learning rate x0.5 / x2, longer warmup)
backlog.why: Pointers only: we keep our own training setup (decision 10-17)

backlog.item: Distill only on users the fork never trained on
backlog.why: Needs a per-user distillation mask

backlog.item: Fork runtime port of the exported format
backlog.why: Specified; Rust vs NumPy within 1e-5

backlog.item: Pruning: depth cut of the deck / preset / user streams (−38% params)
backlog.why: Design written; deprioritised 10-17 in favour of accuracy and speed

backlog.item: w80 student
backlog.why: Only if a capacity limit shows up

backlog.why: Read 10-17; new rows above, plus a list of dead ends to skip

backlog.why: In use since 10-15

results.name: Calibration fitted offline on the dec10 student (temperature + bias, user-split cross-validation)
results.fork: fork 0.29766 / 0.27216 (calibrated the same way: 0.29761 / 0.27214); uncalibrated student 0.30096 / 0.27471
results.takeaway: Nothing to fold into the export: both models are equally (and barely) miscalibrated, gains are ~5e-5. Spaced slice unchanged: +0.79% / +0.84%.
results.label: sm12-calib

results.name: One-epoch final decay at 2,048 windows (vs our quarter epoch)
results.fork: fork 0.29766 / 0.27216; same start with a quarter-epoch decay 0.30259 / 0.27668
results.takeaway: Longer decay helps: −0.00033 curve [−0.00068, −0.00008] / −0.00019 instant [−0.00025, −0.00012] (292 / 351 of 464 users better). Smaller than the gain seen in outside runs; a 1-epoch decay at 32k would cost ~4½ h
results.label: s-w64kd-gate-ctx2048c-dec8-1ep/w8+s8

results.name: Speed check of the compression-in-training GPU kernels
results.fork: seconds per update: plain 1.12, with compression 1.38 (fused kernels), 3.4–3.8 (PyTorch loop)
results.takeaway: Kernels match the reference (max diff 4e-7). Projected decay 85 min vs 64 plain; scheduled after the review-number flags test

results.name: Training speed profile (quiet GPU): student at 2,048 / 8,192 / 16,384 / 32,768 windows and the fork-size model
results.takeaway: Long windows cost the student a lot (5× slower at 32k than at 2,048). The fork-size model at batch 128 trains faster than the student at 16k+ windows, so a label-free fork-size reference is affordable

results.name: Epoch 10 + decay at 32k on your collection
results.takeaway: Slightly better than the previous best (+0.18% / +0.21%). Calibration RMSE(bins) 0.0286 / 0.0207 vs fork 0.0224 / 0.0200

results.name: Fork with review types relabelled by the first-review rule (no learning steps)
results.fork: vs the real fork; new student vs this relabelled fork: +0.65% / +0.48%
results.takeaway: Without the SM-2 learning-step labels the fork loses about half of its lead over the student

results.name: Where the student's gap sits, by inferred stage (epoch 10 + decay)
results.takeaway: Spaced reviews already meet the target on both heads; the curve gap is mostly learning steps (same-day 43% of the gap)

results.name: Extra epoch at 32k windows (epoch 10) + final decay at 32k
results.takeaway: Instant now meets the target (better than the previous best for 341/464 users). Curve slightly worse than the previous best (+0.0003, not significant; 288/464 users better)
results.label: s-w64kd-gate-ctx32768c-dec10/w8+s8

results.name: Epoch 10 at 32k, before decay
results.takeaway: Undecayed; judge after decay
results.label: s-w64kd-gate-ctx32768c-e10/w8+s8

results.name: State compression without retraining: ~800/800 bits per card/note (31.7 MB state for the largest user)
results.takeaway: Near the uncompressed student: +0.0007 / +0.0014 nats. Post-training only; training with it (QAT) should cost less

results.name: State compression without retraining: ~400/400 bits (15.6 MB)
results.takeaway: Best size/accuracy point: +0.0012 / +0.0023 vs uncompressed (959 MB). Post-training only; training with it (QAT) should cost less

results.name: State compression without retraining: the deployed 403/214-bit codec (14.5 MB)
results.takeaway: The 1-bit norms cost most of it; with 4-bit norms +0.0012 / +0.0025. Post-training only; training with it (QAT) should cost less

results.name: Extra epoch at 32k windows (epoch 10), before decay, 100 gate users
results.takeaway: Better than epoch 9 before decay on the same users (+2.68% / +2.51%). The decay result decides
results.label: s-w64kd-gate-ctx32768c-e10/w8+s8

results.name: Best student on your collection (review types not SM-2)
results.takeaway: Almost level with the fork where the SM-2 label is absent. Calibration a bit worse on curve (RMSE(bins) 0.0274 vs 0.0224)

results.name: Fork with review type removed, on your collection
results.takeaway: The fork leans on the labels your fork writes

results.name: Fork with first-review-rule labels, on your collection
results.takeaway: A simple rule costs nothing here

results.name: Fork with history review types rewritten (no learning steps)
results.takeaway: Its curve lead on learning steps disappears: it came from the SM-2 label. Zeroed instead: 0.33569 / 0.28778 (+8.4% / +3.3%)

results.name: Review-number statistics, small correction model, 19 candidate features
results.takeaway: No gain for the student on any slice; the correction model makes unseen users worse

results.name: Gap by review type (student = 8k model decayed at 32k)
results.takeaway: Curve: level on spaced reviews (−0.03%), +1.0 to +1.2% on learning steps. Instant behind everywhere

CPU inference speed
results.takeaway: w64 NumPy step 7.8x faster than the eager fork, 1.84x faster than a NumPy fork (exact to 4e-7)

results.name: In-window check at 2,048 (both models see only 2,048-review windows)
results.takeaway: The gap was missing context, not capacity (full history: +1.98% / +2.40%)

results.name: Per-user view and shared history
results.takeaway: Curve gap on heavy users, closed by longer windows; instant a uniform ~+1.1% on all user sizes. Shared decks do not explain the gap

results.takeaway: Still improving

results.takeaway: Context length is the lever
